topic: Exact joint-response Stieltjes cone for continuous-heterogeneity feedback logit. Let c=exp(theta)>0 and u=exp(alpha) in (0,infinity); fix the full positive sixteen-cell T=2 binary-logit law while initial assignment and feedback may depend arbitrarily on alpha. Prove that the sharp joint slope/APE set is exactly represented by eight joint (X1,r0,r1) response-type measures and a finite open-half-line quartic Stieltjes lift: 56 auxiliary variables with eight 3x3 and eight augmented 4x4 PSD blocks for weak probabilities, and 64 variables with eight additional 6x6 common-Hankel-range blocks for strict positivity. Prove forward/reverse legal-kernel reconstruction, sharp fixed-c infimum/supremum endpoints with separate attainment tests, terminating algebraic membership/projection for algebraic inputs, exact multinomial whole-set coverage, and fixed-c endpoint consistency only on relative-interior attainable laws. Closest work: Bonhomme-Dano-Graham 2023 gives the sharp infinite-dimensional feedback program and grid computation; DGKR 2026 lacks the separate unrestricted feedback kernel. Consumer: replace support-grid robustness bounds in the Arellano-Carrasco PSID predetermined-children labor-participation design. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Eight measures with densities h_x g_x0(r0) g_x1(r1) preserve one unconditional law and admit Radon-Nikodym reconstruction; the common quartic denominator leaves five bounded moments per type. Independent rank-by-rank checks support the augmented positive-half-line Stieltjes certificate and equal-Hankel-range common-support criterion. Exact arithmetic verifies a positive c=2 witness with Delta=3/20 and every stated PSD block, and destructive checks cover zero/one/two/full-rank, escape-to-infinity, c=1 rank loss, nonattainment, and weak-infeasibility regimes. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: No unresolved theorem step remains within the stated scope; continuity at strictly positive relative-boundary laws and joint consistency through c=1 are explicitly excluded extensions. EARLY KILL TEST: Reconstruct legal positive-node measures on zero-only, zero-plus-positive, one-node, two-node, and full-rank moment inputs, checking both augmented range conditions and common support whenever all eight Hankel ranges agree; any feasible lifted vector without a legal feedback reconstruction kills the theorem. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/pid_feedback_logit_stieltjes_cone.md

open_problems.open_problem: Does the two-period binary feedback-logit model with continuous heterogeneity admit an exact finite Stieltjes-cone characterization of the joint slope-APE identified set that remains sharp when outcome or feedback cells have zero probability?

source_refs.claim: The continuous-heterogeneity sharp program is infinite-dimensional and computed on finite grids; non-interior feedback processes are left for future work.
source_refs.author: Stéphane Bonhomme, Kevin Dano, and Bryan S. Graham

source_refs.claim: Dynamic-logit identification with unrestricted fixed-effect distributions is reduced to truncated-Stieltjes equalities and PSD constraints, but without a separately reconstructed unrestricted feedback kernel.
source_refs.author: Christopher Dobronyi, Jiaying Gu, Kyoo il Kim, and Thomas M. Russell

open_problems.why_unsolved: Bonhomme-Dano-Graham formulate the sharp unrestricted-feedback problem but approximate continuous heterogeneity by grids and exclude non-interior feedback, while Dobronyi-Gu-Kim-Russell provide finite Stieltjes machinery only after conditioning on covariate histories. Joining the strands requires replacing a conditional fixed-effect law by joint response-type measures and proving that singular Hankel-face and common-support conditions suffice for Radon-Nikodym reconstruction of one unconditional heterogeneity law and legal feedback kernels. Searches combining dynamic logit, Stieltjes moments, and unrestricted feedback found the two components but no such reconstruction result.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if finite PSD/range characterization of attainable cell laws and joint slope-APE values, with forward and reverse legal-kernel reconstruction and exact fixed-slope endpoint-attainment conditions.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from economically natural feedback to partial identification and computable slope and APE sets.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Predetermined states respond to past choices -> unrestricted heterogeneity and feedback defeat point identification -> sharp continuous-heterogeneity slope and APE sets need an exact non-grid representation

method_exemplars.technique: Factor logistic history probabilities through a common rational denominator, map generalized moments to truncated Stieltjes sequences, and prove representability with Hankel PSD and range conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested lift has the same rational-mixture and positive-half-line moment structure, with response-type feedback measures and common-support reconstruction added.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate conditional probabilities, impose semidefinite generalized-moment restrictions, and invert a constrained test statistic for set-identified parameters.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest existing estimation and test-inversion pipeline for a dynamic-logit identified set represented by PSD moment constraints.

open_problems.open_problem: Under first-order Markov feedback, what is the sharp joint identified set for the predetermined-covariate slope and its APE when conditional likelihood cannot identify that slope?

source_refs.claim: Markov feedback makes the response-function restrictions nonlinear, and sharp identification under that restriction is left for future work.
source_refs.author: Stéphane Bonhomme, Kevin Dano, and Bryan S. Graham

source_refs.claim: With a general first-order Markov covariate process, sufficient-statistic conditional likelihood can identify state dependence but not the covariate coefficient.
source_refs.author: Sukgyu Shin

open_problems.why_unsolved: The sufficient-statistic result identifies which coefficients survive conditioning, but failure of that argument for the covariate slope is not a sharp-set characterization. Bonhomme-Dano-Graham locate the missing step: equality of a Markov feedback kernel across histories imposes nonlinear ratios of response measures. Those ratio restrictions, including zero denominators, must be translated into polynomial or rank-compatible moment constraints without silently imposing interior transition probabilities; targeted searches found no sharp joint slope-APE bounds that do so.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp semialgebraic or moment-cone characterization of all slope-APE pairs compatible with the observed panel law and a first-order Markov feedback kernel, including a regime-by-regime treatment of zero transition cells.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames Markov feedback through sufficient statistics and pinpoints the coefficient for which conditional likelihood fails.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Markov feedback is economically structured -> sufficient statistics remove some nuisance components -> the covariate slope remains unidentified -> characterize its sharp joint set with the APE

method_exemplars.technique: Factor likelihoods into sufficient statistics for individual heterogeneity and transition kernels, then compare histories within nuisance-statistic cells.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The factorization cells expose the cross-history equalities that a sharp-set formulation must retain rather than condition away.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode rational logistic mixtures by generalized moments and enforce representability with Stieltjes Hankel PSD and range restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After imposing Markov polynomial equalities, each response-measure marginal still has the same univariate positive-half-line moment structure.

method_exemplars.technique: Characterize feedback-and-heterogeneity-robust moments and their efficiency bound, then construct feasible moment estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies feedback-robust sampling theory for the same slope and average-effect objects, complementing a new sharp-set characterization.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the exact finite Stieltjes representation for unrestricted-feedback dynamic logit be extended from two periods to arbitrary fixed T with an explicit complexity bound and constructive common-kernel reconstruction?

source_refs.claim: Non-point-identification is proved for every finite T and identified sets are formulated by linear programming, while continuous-heterogeneity calculations use finite support grids.
source_refs.author: Stéphane Bonhomme, Kevin Dano, and Bryan S. Graham

source_refs.claim: Without a separately modeled unrestricted feedback kernel, dynamic fixed-effects logit has finitely many generalized moments whose number grows linearly with T.
source_refs.author: Christopher Dobronyi, Jiaying Gu, Kyoo il Kim, and Thomas M. Russell

source_refs.claim: Rational-fraction transition-probability methods generate fixed-effect-free restrictions that scale systematically with lag order and panel length.
source_refs.author: Kevin Dano

open_problems.why_unsolved: For larger T, the unrestricted feedback tree creates many history-indexed response measures while the logistic likelihood creates higher-degree common denominators. The first changed proof step is not just a larger Hankel matrix: one must find a minimal moment collection shared across exponentially many histories and show that all locally reconstructed atomic measures arise from one unconditional heterogeneity distribution and legal sequential feedback kernels. Searches found arbitrary-T infinite programs and arbitrary-T rational/Stieltjes constructions separately, but no finite exact unrestricted-feedback synthesis or lift-size bound.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A fixed-T theorem giving an explicit finite family of linear, Hankel-PSD, and range constraints equivalent to the model, an algorithm reconstructing the common heterogeneity and feedback kernels, and a proved bound on lift dimension and block sizes.

writing_exemplar.why: Its all-finite-T nonidentification result and numerical comparisons motivate replacing increasingly expensive grids by an exact scalable representation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Feedback prevents point identification at every finite T -> added periods still shrink the set -> continuous heterogeneity remains an infinite program -> obtain an exact finite representation with transparent T-complexity

method_exemplars.technique: Use rational-fraction operations on transition probabilities to generate restrictions recursively as lag order and T increase.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired arbitrary-T denominator and moment bookkeeping is the same recursion applied to feedback-response measures.

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce a general-T rational mixture to finitely many generalized moments and prove Stieltjes representability with PSD and singular-range conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates finite moment growth before the additional feedback-compatibility restrictions are imposed.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply semidefinite set estimation and test inversion to generalized-moment constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the nearest estimator and confidence-set theory for the proposed arbitrary-T finite lift.

open_problems.open_problem: Can fixed-slope joint slope-APE endpoint inference be made uniformly valid for relative-boundary attainable laws and local sequences through c=1 under primitive first-stage or IPCW learner conditions?

source_refs.claim: The paper provides consistency and test-inversion inference for dynamic-logit sets under regularity and tuning conditions, with PSD restrictions implemented through principal minors.
source_refs.author: Christopher Dobronyi, Jiaying Gu, Kyoo il Kim, and Thomas M. Russell

source_refs.claim: The paper obtains root-n outer bounds and asymptotically valid confidence intervals for average effects because sharp-set estimation can be impractical.
source_refs.author: Cavit Pakel and Martin Weidner
source_refs.venue: Review of Economics and Statistics, conditionally accepted

source_refs.claim: The paper develops consistent estimators and confidence regions for identified sets defined by criterion equalities and inequalities.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Han Hong, and Elie Tamer

source_refs.excerpt: This is an additional primitive learner restriction; it is not imposed by Westling et al.'s generic nuisance metrics.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic set-inference results do not handle a Stieltjes lift whose active PSD face and Hankel rank change with the observed law, whose rational parameterization loses rank at c=1, and whose cell-law estimate may itself use learned IPCW weights. The prior writeup isolates an analogous need for an extra primitive learner restriction to control a Stieltjes remainder, while the web literature supplies only regular SDP inference or stable outer bounds. The first failed step is a uniform error bound and stochastic expansion when endpoint attainment switches, common-denominator rank changes, or nuisance perturbations move the estimated law across a semidefinite face.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A local-sequence theorem giving uniform set or endpoint coverage and an explicit asymptotic linear or directional limit law across stated relative-boundary strata and c_n approaching 1, under primitive nuisance classes and product-rate conditions.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents identification, computation, consistency, and test inversion as one pipeline, making the missing boundary-uniform extension precise.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Finite moment constraints make exact set computation possible -> empirical cell laws must be estimated -> regular SDP inference is available -> rank-changing boundary laws, learned weights, and c=1 require uniform endpoint theory

method_exemplars.technique: Construct criterion-based set estimators and confidence regions by controlling stochastic criterion errors and separation from the identified set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result requires a rank-stratified verification of this set-estimation argument for a nonregular semidefinite feasible correspondence.

method_exemplars.technique: Use constrained minimum-distance statistics over generalized moments and test inversion for dynamic-logit confidence sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives the model-specific stochastic program to retain while replacing interior regularity by rank-stratified analysis.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct parametric-rate outer-bound estimators and asymptotically valid confidence intervals for panel average effects.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its stable outer region is a natural benchmark when exact endpoint geometry is nonregular.

open_problems.open_problem: Does a dynamic multinomial-logit panel with a discrete predetermined covariate, unrestricted continuous heterogeneity, and unrestricted feedback admit a sharp finite moment or sums-of-squares characterization of joint slope and average-effect sets?

source_refs.claim: The rational transition-probability construction covers dynamic multinomial logit but assumes strictly exogenous regressors and treats average effects chiefly for the binary case.
source_refs.author: Kevin Dano

source_refs.claim: Sharp unrestricted-feedback slope and APE programs are developed for a binary outcome and a binary predetermined covariate.
source_refs.author: Stéphane Bonhomme, Kevin Dano, and Bryan S. Graham

source_refs.claim: Conditional-likelihood identification in structural multinomial dynamic logit uses sufficient statistics for fixed heterogeneity rather than unrestricted feedback.
source_refs.author: Victor Aguirregabiria, Jiaying Gu, and Yao Luo

open_problems.why_unsolved: The binary unrestricted-feedback construction and the multinomial strictly-exogenous rational construction occupy opposite sides of the target. With three or more choices, the first proof step changes from a univariate odds variable and scalar Stieltjes sequence to several positive odds coordinates and a multivariate truncated moment problem; scalar Hankel PSD conditions no longer suffice, and compatibility of category-specific feedback measures must also be proved. Targeted searches returned multinomial fixed-effects and sufficient-statistic papers but no sharp continuous-heterogeneity unrestricted-feedback joint-set result.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either an exact finite multivariate-moment or SOS lift with legal-kernel reconstruction and sharp joint slope-average-effect projection, or a counterexample showing that no bounded-order finite lift characterizes a stated multinomial regime.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates multinomial dynamic logit through state dependence and gives the closest scalable rational formulation while marking its strict-exogeneity scope.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Multinomial choices exhibit state dependence -> transition probabilities have exploitable rational structure -> current constructions assume strict exogeneity -> unrestricted feedback needs a multivariate sharp-set representation

method_exemplars.technique: Generate multinomial fixed-effect-free restrictions by rational manipulation of category transition probabilities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the numerator and denominator algebra that must be translated into multivariate moments before feedback compatibility is imposed.

method_exemplars.technique: Prove sharpness of rational-mixture restrictions through truncated-moment representability instead of discretizing heterogeneity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its univariate proof is the structural template whose replacement in several odds coordinates is the central mathematical problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate and form confidence regions for sets defined by finite equality and inequality criterion functions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A finite SOS or moment lift would induce exactly such a profiled criterion for joint multinomial slopes and average effects.

open_problems.open_problem: Are the sign and magnitude conclusions for predetermined children's effect on female labor-force participation in the PSID robust under the sharp joint slope-APE set with unrestricted heterogeneity and feedback?

source_refs.claim: The PSID application estimates female participation with predetermined children using a GMM model that restricts dependence on individual effects through a conditional-mean specification.
source_refs.author: Manuel Arellano and Raquel Carrasco

source_refs.claim: A later PSID conditional-likelihood analysis reports no evidence that female employment feeds back into fertility or husband's income under restrictions on the covariate distribution.
source_refs.author: Claudia Pigini and Francesco Bartolucci

source_refs.claim: Allowing arbitrary feedback and unrestricted heterogeneity generally destroys point identification but can leave informative joint coefficient and APE sets.
source_refs.author: Stéphane Bonhomme, Kevin Dano, and Bryan S. Graham

open_problems.why_unsolved: The two PSID analyses reach conclusions under different restrictions on heterogeneity and the feedback law, while Bonhomme-Dano-Graham show that relaxing those restrictions turns point identification into a sharp-set problem. A grid sensitivity exercise cannot certify whether the sign, the no-feedback submodel, or a reported APE survives continuous heterogeneity. The first changed step is to map the empirical cell-frequency law into an exact feasible response-measure cone and then propagate sampling uncertainty through its endpoint programs.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A PSID-design-specific sharp identified region and valid confidence region for the children slope and labor-participation APE, including formal tests of whether zero effect and the no-feedback submodel intersect the attainable set.

writing_exemplar.why: It establishes the economic question, data construction, and interpretation of predetermined children in the PSID.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Children and participation may affect each other over time -> strict exogeneity is implausible -> the original PSID design uses a restricted correlated-effects GMM model -> reassess the same effect under unrestricted feedback with sharp bounds

method_exemplars.technique: Represent unrestricted feedback and heterogeneity by response functions and optimize coefficient and APE functionals over observationally equivalent laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the robust identifying model that replaces the conditional-mean and exponential-family feedback restrictions in the PSID studies.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct computationally tractable bounds and asymptotically valid confidence intervals for average effects in short discrete-choice panels.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It includes a female-labor-participation application and provides the nearest coverage-facing analysis of panel average-effect bounds.

method_exemplars.technique: Perform estimation and test inversion subject to semidefinite moment-representability constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest inferential implementation if the unrestricted-feedback PSID set has an exact Stieltjes lift.

literature_map:
1. Arellano and Carrasco (2003, Journal of Econometrics) model predetermined children and female PSID participation, but restrict dependence on heterogeneity through a conditional-mean specification.
2. Honoré and Tamer (2006, Econometrica) give constructive bounds for dynamic discrete-choice panels and show that non-point-identified regions can nevertheless be narrow.
3. Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham (2023, SERIEs; arXiv:2301.05733) allow unrestricted heterogeneity and feedback, prove broad nonidentification, and formulate sharp slope and APE programs.
4. Their continuous-heterogeneity calculations remain grid approximations, and they leave non-interior feedback and sharp analysis under nonlinear Markov restrictions unresolved.
5. Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell (2026, Review of Economic Studies forthcoming; arXiv:2104.04590) connect dynamic logit to truncated Stieltjes moments and obtain finite PSD characterizations plus SDP inference.
6. Their baseline conditions on covariate histories do not reconstruct the separate unrestricted feedback kernel required by the Bonhomme-Dano-Graham program.
7. Honoré and Weidner (2024, Review of Economic Studies; arXiv:2005.05942) derive analytic moments and root-n GMM identification under strictly exogenous regressors.
8. Dano (2025 working paper; arXiv:2303.00083) develops scalable rational-fraction restrictions for arbitrary lag order and dynamic multinomial logit, again under strict exogeneity.
9. Bonhomme, Dano, and Graham (2025/2026, R&R Econometrica; arXiv:2506.12569) characterize feedback-and-heterogeneity-robust moments and efficiency bounds, but do not replace sharp latent-law set analysis.
10. Shin (2025; arXiv:2511.02816) uses sufficient statistics under first-order Markov feedback: state dependence may be identified, whereas the general covariate slope is not recovered by conditional likelihood.
11. Pakel and Weidner (2026, Review of Economics and Statistics conditionally accepted; arXiv:2309.09299) trade sharpness for tractable root-n outer bounds and confidence intervals for panel average effects.
12. Aguirregabiria and Carro (2024/2025, Review of Economics and Statistics forthcoming; arXiv:2107.06141) identify dynamic-logit average marginal effects from choice histories under stronger fixed-effects structure.
13. Pigini and Bartolucci (2022, Econometrics and Statistics) report no PSID fertility-feedback evidence under an exponential-family conditional-likelihood model, creating a robustness tension with unrestricted feedback.
14. Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007, Econometrica) provide general criterion-based set-estimation and confidence-region machinery for an exact feedback cone.
15. Searches combining unrestricted feedback with Stieltjes moments, multinomial outcomes, non-interior cells, or rank-changing inference found these components but no paper joining them into an exact sharp joint slope-APE result.
